caption: LUM-1267 interaction assertions (120x34). Run against a binary built from feature/pi.rs; every panel asserts the interaction a codex/pi-class TUI owes the user.
notes: Assertion kinds: expect/reject gate the run; probe records A/B evidence (XFAIL when a binary does not have a behaviour yet); xfail/xfail_reject are markers for known defects and fail the run when they unexpectedly pass.

Panels 3-4 document the completion filter's over-broad candidate set (LUM-1260 §2): `mo` matches substring in the description too, upstream matches the name only, so those needles are xfail_reject — they must move to `reject` when LUM-1263 lands.

Panel 15 asserts the /help body only; the wrap/clipping questions (LUM-1261 §7.1, LUM-1266 §B) are asserted by the pi-tui tests and the lum1261/lum1266 scenarios, because they pin exact column arithmetic that only the unit tests can state.
Panel 8 is legitimately byte-identical to panel 6 (closing the model-selector overlay returns to the same placeholder frame); the harness prints that as a WARN, not a failure.

panels.label: 1. idle: product line, hint table, onboarding line, composer placeholder, status line
expect: Pi can explain its own features

panels.label: 2. type / -> the command completion opens with a live counter and the first candidate selected
3. type mo -> /model stays selected and the over-broad candidate set is visible (see the xfail_reject markers)

xfail_reject.text: Copy last agent message to clipboard
xfail_reject.why: LUM-1263: upstream filters candidates by command name only; matching the description too is a deviation and must go

xfail_reject.text: Create a new fork from a previous user message

panels.label: 4. Down -> the selection marker moves to the next candidate and the counter agrees
5. Tab -> the selected candidate is applied to the composer and the list closes

reject.why: the completion list must be gone once a candidate is accepted

panels.label: 6. Enter -> the slash command runs and reports its result in the transcript
7. /model + Enter -> the model selector overlay lists real models with their providers
8. Esc -> the overlay closes and the composer is back to its placeholder
9. @ -> file-path completion over the fixture tree, with paths resolved relative to the cwd
10. src -> candidates narrow to that subtree; the unfiltered fixtures are gone
11. Tab -> the path token is composed into the composer and the list closes
12. a real turn through the provider: the prompt and the reply both land in the transcript
13. !bash -> the command, its output and its duration are reported as one tool block
14. Ctrl+O -> the status line reports the tool-output expansion state
15. /help -> the slash-command reference renders into the transcript
16. /hotkeys -> the chord table renders into the transcript
expect: Esc close the selector / overlay first

panels.label: 17. PgUp -> the transcript scrolls back and the jump-to-latest pill appears
